chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq from Ali ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Dawud al-Raqqi who said:

We were sitting with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when a man passed by with a snipe in his hand, slaughtered. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) jumped at it until he took it from his hand, then threw it down, and said, 'Has your scholar commanded you to do this, or your jurist? My father informed me from my grandfather that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade the killing of six creatures: the bee, the ant, the frog, the hoopoe, and the snipe.'

key_terms.الْهُدْهُد: Hoopoe (often used interchangeably or distinctly depending on context, here listed alongside)

ai.seo_question: What are the six animals forbidden to be killed according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) uses the sight of a slaughtered snipe to critique the practical application of fiqh by contemporary scholars, linking it to a Prophetic tradition transmitted through his forefathers. This hadith highlights the specific prohibition of six animals—snipe, bee, ant, frog, hoopoe, and sandgrouse—emphasizing a holistic view of creation where even small creatures are protected from unnecessary harm, a principle deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence regarding animal rights.
